## Turn Priority Acoustic Gaps into Testable Changes

**Kaizen** means improving a research workflow through small, incremental, scientist-led changes[cite: 8]. Instead of committing to massive, unproven software overhauls or costly custom hardware builds, passive acoustics research teams run limited, measurable experiments—such as piloting a deep-learning classifier on a single cruise leg or testing automated clock-drift scripts on two glider deployments[cite: 8]. In Value Stream Mapping (VSM), this continuous-improvement practice converts identified gaps between Current and Future States into concrete, scientific action[cite: 8].

Start with high-priority analyst bottlenecks, validate the baseline processing times ($PT$) and accuracy rates (%C&A) with the staff performing the work, and choose the smallest safe pilot test to evaluate your hypothesis[cite: 8].

---

## The PDCA Cycle for Bioacoustic Pipelines

The **Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA)** cycle provides a rigorous, scientific framework for testing pipeline improvements[cite: 8]:

| Stage | What the Research Team Does | PAM Pipeline Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Plan** | Select a verified gap, describe the change as a testable hypothesis, choose a success metric (e.g., $PT$ in hr/TB or %C&A), and assign an owner and pilot scope[cite: 8]. | Formulate hypothesis: *"Deploying a pre-trained deep learning model for baleen whale detections will cut analyst validation time by 50% without reducing recall below 90%"*[cite: 8]. |
| **Do** | Run the smallest safe pilot test and record execution logs, compute resources used, and analyst effort[cite: 8]. | Run the new model on 2 bottom-mounted mooring datasets (approx. 2 TB) alongside standard manual review[cite: 8]. |
| **Check** | Compare measured pilot results against baseline metrics, checking for false positives, processing speed, and metadata integrity[cite: 8]. | Evaluate model precision/recall, compare analyst review hours against the baseline, and audit NCEI schema compliance[cite: 8]. |
| **Act** | Adopt a successful script/workflow, adapt parameters based on pilot findings, or abandon an ineffective approach[cite: 8]. | If validated, deploy the classifier across the full annual mooring dataset and establish a new Current State baseline[cite: 8]. |

PDCA is a continuous cycle[cite: 8]. Successful pilot results update your Future State target or establish a modernized baseline for future research projects[cite: 8].

---

## Core Inputs and Outputs

| File | Role in the Experiment Cycle |
|---|---|
| `gap-analysis.csv` / `prioritized-experiments.csv` | Supplies verified process gaps, baselines, targets, priorities, and source timestamps for starting experiment cards[cite: 7, 8]. |
| `kaizen-experiments.json` | Preserves the complete experiment roadmap, nested action-step checklists, and pilot logs for later workspace reloads[cite: 8]. |
| `kaizen-experiments.csv` | Provides a structured, flat roadmap for project reporting, team reviews, and executive management updates[cite: 8]. |

All files are processed locally inside your web browser[cite: 8]. Save or move downloaded exports into `output/` so the experiment history remains preserved alongside the rest of your VSM project assets[cite: 8].

---

## From Acoustic Gap to Pilot Experiment

1. Import `gap-analysis.csv` (or `prioritized-experiments.csv`) into the [interactive workspace](./kaizen-primary.qmd)[cite: 7, 8].
2. Review generated experiment cards and refine each hypothesis for your bioacoustic workflow[cite: 8].
3. Assign a lead bioacoustician/engineer, action checklist, priority ranking, and target success metrics[cite: 8].
4. Track progress through **Backlog / Proposed**, **In Progress / Pilot Test**, **Testing / Verification**, and **Completed / Operationalized**[cite: 8].
5. Export the updated roadmap as `kaizen-experiments.json` or `kaizen-experiments.csv` into `output/`[cite: 8].
